question: Which 4.100.108 functions implement the NuttX semaphore wait/post/trywait primitives?
prototype_hypothesis: sem_wait(sem) blocks until the semaphore count is positive (with priority-inheritance list insertion); sem_post(sem) releases the semaphore and wakes the highest-priority waiter; sem_trywait(sem) returns immediately with EBUSY if the count is zero.
callsite_evidence: sub_C359510 (candidate sem_wait) decompiles to the canonical NuttX sem_wait and references "../../nuttx/sched/semaphore/sem_wait.c" and "../../nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h"; it uses the hardware spinlock/atomic path (LDAEXH/STLEXH, BASEPRI manipulation), the priority-inheritance waiting list insert, and the linux_eabi_syscall scheduler handoff

sub_C359470 (candidate sem_trywait) and sub_C359980 (candidate sem_post) share the same NuttX semaphore core helpers (sub_C354AF0 list-wake, the sched_lock region byte_200AD130) and the same spinlock pattern
The three candidates sit in the same XIP cluster as the 3.101.036 sem_* wrappers and were produced by the multi-layer matcher, then confirmed by decompiling the exact 4.100.108 IDB
control_flow_evidence: sem_wait first checks the semaphore count via an atomic decrement; on failure it links the waiting TCB into the priority-ordered list (offset +4/+8 of the semaphore) and calls the scheduler handoff, returning -v12[35] (the saved errno) on timeout
sem_post releases the count and wakes the waiter with the highest priority via the list-wake helper sub_C354AF0
sem_trywait performs the same atomic check without blocking, returning immediately on a zero count
ownership_analysis: Semaphores are caller-owned; the wrappers touch the NuttX global scheduler state (dword_200AEE0C g_readytorun) and must run in a scheduler-aware context. Suitable for target-private thread synchronization.
unsafe_assumptions: The scheduler global offsets (dword_200AEE0C + 27/+11/+35, byte_200AD130) are recovered from this exact IDB and are BES1503 NuttX layout specifics
sem_post may run in an interrupt/worker context; callers must match the 036 facade contract for allowed contexts
recommended_probe: Exercise sem_wait/sem_post/sem_trywait through the target-private facade from a worker thread and confirm blocking, waking, and EBUSY behavior.
